purpose: Metronidazole is used to treat infections caused by certain bacteria and parasites. It can treat infections in your stomach, intestines, skin, vagina, and other parts of the body. Your doctor may also prescribe it for conditions like bacterial vaginosis or certain stomach ulcer-related infections.
how_it_works: Metronidazole works by entering the harmful bacteria or parasites and damaging their DNA so they can no longer grow or survive. Think of it like cutting the power source that keeps the germs alive. This allows your body's immune system to clear up the infection more easily.
common_side_effects: Nausea, upset stomach, loss of appetite, a metallic or bitter taste in your mouth, dry mouth, headache, and dizziness. Some people may notice darker urine, which is harmless. If taken as a vaginal gel or cream, you may notice mild irritation.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication and for at least 48 hours after finishing it — mixing the two can cause severe nausea, vomiting, flushing, and rapid heartbeat. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, especially in the first trimester. Let your doctor know if you have liver disease, nerve problems, or a history of seizures. This medicine may cause dizziness, so be careful driving.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the type of infection being treated. A common adult dose is 500 mg taken by mouth two to three times a day, usually for 5 to 10 days. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed, finish the full course even if you feel better, and try to take it with food to reduce stomach upset.
